history: Found as a live off-by-one. js/src/canonical.js counted containers and refused above 32; canonical.py started _check_shape at depth 0 on the top-level object and bounded the deepest value, which admitted 33 containers whenever the innermost was empty -- so Python and Rust loaded a document the npm parser refused. MAX_DEPTH was 32 in both files and meant two different things. Settled on the container count, which is the rule a reader can state without reading the code.
note: 33 nested containers with an empty innermost. 32 loads everywhere; this refuses everywhere. The empty innermost is the whole point of the vector: a depth rule that measures the deepest VALUE rather than the container nesting reads this document as one level shallower than it is.
